etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Anglo-Norman vigrus, from Old French vigoros (French vigoureux), from Medieval Latin vigorosus, from Latin vigor. Doublet of vigoroso.

quote.citation: 1895, Annual Report of the Ohio State Board of Agriculture, page 280:
quote.text: Life in the country will be fuller, richer, and more comfortful, because it is freer, healthier, and more vigorous.

quote.citation: 1976, Joni Mitchell (lyrics and music), “Song for Sharon”:
quote.text: Now there are twenty-nine skaters on Wollman RinkCircling in singles and in pairsIn this vigorous anonymity
